5-1.title: Earth's Interior
5-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Earth is made of layers, like a ball with a hard shell and a hot center. From outside to inside:
- Crust: the thin, solid OUTER layer we live on (land and ocean floor).
- Mantle: the thick, hot layer of solid rock that can slowly FLOW over long times.
- Core: the center, made of two parts — a LIQUID metal outer core and a SOLID metal inner core (it stays solid because of enormous pressure).

General rule: the DEEPER you go, the HOTTER and DENSER it gets.

Example 1 — Order of layers
From the surface down: crust → mantle → outer core → inner core.

Example 2 — Why the inner core is solid
The inner core is extremely hot but stays solid because the crushing pressure deep inside Earth keeps the metal packed tightly.

Example 3 — Thinnest vs. thickest
The crust is the thinnest layer; the mantle is the thickest layer.

questions.question: The state of matter of the inner core is

questions.explanation: The inner core is deep inside Earth and much hotter than the crust, since temperature rises with depth.

5-2.title: Earth's Spheres Interacting
5-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Earth is made of connected systems called spheres:
- Geosphere: the solid rock and land.
- Hydrosphere: all the liquid water (oceans, rivers, lakes).
- Cryosphere: the frozen ice and snow (glaciers, sea ice).
- Atmosphere: the layer of air (gases) around Earth.
- Biosphere: all living things (plants, animals, people, microbes).

These spheres constantly INTERACT — an event in one sphere affects others. Earth works as ONE big connected system.

Example 1 — Rain wears down a mountain
Rain (hydrosphere) wears down rock (geosphere) and gives water to plants (biosphere) — three spheres interacting.

Example 2 — A tree's roots
A tree (biosphere) takes water (hydrosphere) and breaks apart rock with its roots (geosphere), and gives off gases into the air (atmosphere).

Example 3 — Match the sphere
A glacier = cryosphere. The ocean = hydrosphere. Soil and mountains = geosphere. A flock of birds = biosphere. Clouds and wind = atmosphere.

questions.explanation: The hydrosphere is all the liquid water on Earth, such as oceans, rivers, and lakes.

questions.explanation: The geosphere is the solid rock and land of Earth.

questions.explanation: The biosphere includes all living things — plants, animals, people, and microbes.

questions.explanation: The atmosphere is the layer of gases (air) surrounding Earth.

questions.explanation: Rain (hydrosphere) wearing down rock (geosphere) is an interaction between those two spheres.

questions.question: Plants taking in water from the soil shows an interaction between the
questions.explanation: Plants (biosphere) taking in water (hydrosphere) is an interaction between those two spheres.

choices.B: Because a change in one sphere can affect the others

choices.D: Because the spheres are all made of water

questions.explanation: The spheres constantly interact, so a change in one affects the others, making Earth one connected system.

questions.explanation: The volcano (geosphere) sends ash into the air (atmosphere) and harms plants (biosphere), so three spheres interact.

questions.question: The frozen ice and snow on Earth, such as glaciers and sea ice, make up the
questions.explanation: The cryosphere is Earth's frozen ice and snow, including glaciers and sea ice.

questions.question: Mountains and soil are part of which sphere?
questions.explanation: Mountains and soil are solid rock and land, which make up the geosphere.

questions.explanation: The glacier (cryosphere) wearing away the rock (geosphere) is an interaction between those two spheres.

questions.question: Which best describes the biosphere?

choices.A: All the liquid water on Earth
choices.B: All the rock and land on Earth

questions.explanation: The biosphere includes all living things — plants, animals, people, and microbes.

questions.question: Snow on a mountain melts and flows into a river. This shows a change from the
questions.explanation: Frozen snow (cryosphere) melting into flowing water (hydrosphere) shows a change between those two spheres.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches an item with its sphere?
questions.explanation: A glacier is frozen ice, which belongs to the cryosphere.

questions.question: Earthworms (living things) digging through soil and rock is an interaction between the
questions.explanation: Earthworms (biosphere) moving through soil and rock (geosphere) is an interaction between those two spheres.

questions.question: Why is it useful to think of Earth as one connected system?

choices.B: Because a change in one sphere can cause changes in the others

questions.explanation: Thinking of Earth as one system helps us see how a change in one sphere can affect the others.

questions.question: A wildfire burns a forest, sends smoke into the air, and chars the soil. Which spheres interact?
questions.explanation: The fire burns the forest (biosphere), sends smoke into the air (atmosphere), and chars the soil (geosphere), so three spheres interact.

questions.question: Which is an EXAMPLE of the geosphere?

questions.question: How is the geosphere DIFFERENT from the atmosphere?

choices.A: The geosphere is solid rock and land, while the atmosphere is air
choices.B: The geosphere is air, while the atmosphere is water
choices.C: The geosphere is living things, while the atmosphere is rock
choices.D: They are both made of ice

questions.question: Sea ice (cryosphere) melting and adding water to the ocean (hydrosphere) shows that

choices.D: the ocean is part of the geosphere

questions.explanation: Melting sea ice adding to the ocean shows how one sphere can change another.

questions.question: Which statement about Earth's spheres is FALSE?

choices.C: The spheres never affect one another
choices.D: The atmosphere is made of gases

questions.explanation: The spheres do affect one another; saying they never interact is false.

questions.question: Ocean water (hydrosphere) evaporating and forming clouds (atmosphere) is an interaction between the

questions.question: Which scenario shows the MOST spheres interacting?

choices.A: A rock sits still on the ground
choices.B: Rain falls, fills a river, and animals drink the water while a tree's roots break nearby rock
choices.C: A cloud floats in the sky

questions.explanation: Rain (hydrosphere), the river, animals and the tree (biosphere), and the broken rock (geosphere) show many spheres interacting at once.

choices.A: geosphere, because the water is held in the ground
choices.B: cryosphere, because the water is frozen
choices.C: atmosphere, because the water is a gas

questions.question: Which item belongs to the hydrosphere?
questions.explanation: A lake of liquid water belongs to the hydrosphere.

questions.question: A bird builds a nest from twigs and mud and breathes the air. Which spheres does the bird connect?
questions.explanation: The bird (biosphere) uses twigs and mud (geosphere) and breathes air (atmosphere), connecting three spheres.

5-3.title: Energy from the Sun
5-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS

The Sun is the main source of energy for almost everything on Earth.

Because Earth is ROUND (curved), the Sun heats different places by different amounts:
- The EQUATOR gets the most DIRECT sunlight, so it is warmest.
- The POLES get sunlight at a slanted angle, spread over more area, so they get LESS heat and are colder.

This UNEVEN heating makes air and water move, creating WIND, OCEAN CURRENTS, and WEATHER. Also, land, water, and air heat up and cool down at different speeds, which adds to these patterns (land heats and cools faster than water).

Example 1 — Why the equator is hot
The equator receives direct, concentrated sunlight, while the poles receive slanted, spread-out sunlight, so the equator is much warmer.

Example 2 — Wind from uneven heating
Warm air near the equator rises and cooler air moves in to replace it; this movement of air is wind, caused by the Sun's uneven heating.

Example 3 — Land vs. water
On a sunny day the sand at a beach gets hot quickly while the ocean water stays cooler, because land heats up faster than water.

questions.question: What is the main source of energy for almost everything on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the main source of energy for nearly all of Earth's processes.

questions.question: Which part of Earth receives the most direct sunlight?
questions.explanation: Because Earth is curved, the equator receives the most direct sunlight and is warmest.

questions.question: Why are the poles colder than the equator?

choices.A: They are closer to the Sun
choices.B: Sunlight hits them at a slanted angle and spreads out
choices.C: The Sun does not shine there at all

questions.explanation: At the poles, sunlight arrives slanted and spread over more area, so it delivers less heat than at the equator.

questions.question: The Sun's uneven heating of Earth helps create
questions.explanation: Uneven heating makes air and water move, producing wind, ocean currents, and weather.

questions.question: Why does the Sun heat Earth unevenly?

choices.B: Earth is round, so sunlight strikes some places more directly than others
choices.D: The Sun turns off at night

questions.explanation: Earth's round shape means sunlight strikes the equator more directly than the poles, causing uneven heating.

questions.question: On a sunny day, the sand at a beach gets hot faster than the ocean water because

choices.A: water heats up faster than land
choices.B: land heats up faster than water
choices.C: the sand is closer to the Sun

questions.explanation: Land heats up (and cools down) faster than water, so the sand gets hot more quickly than the ocean.

questions.question: Wind is mostly caused by

choices.B: the uneven heating of Earth's air by the Sun

questions.explanation: The Sun heats Earth's air unevenly, causing it to move; this moving air is wind.

questions.question: Ocean currents are driven in part by

choices.D: the color of the water only

questions.explanation: Uneven heating of ocean water by the Sun helps drive ocean currents.

questions.question: Which best explains why land near the equator is generally warmer year-round?

choices.A: It is farther from the Sun
choices.B: It receives more direct, concentrated sunlight

questions.explanation: The equator gets direct, concentrated sunlight all year, keeping it warm.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how the Sun affects Earth's weather?

choices.A: The Sun heats Earth evenly, so there is no weather
choices.B: Uneven solar heating moves air and water, creating weather patterns
choices.C: The Sun only heats the poles
choices.D: The Sun has no effect on weather

questions.explanation: The Sun heats Earth unevenly, which moves air and water and creates wind, currents, and weather.

questions.question: Which location gets sunlight at a slanted angle, making it colder?
questions.explanation: The poles receive slanted, spread-out sunlight, so they get less heat and are colder.

questions.question: Moving air across Earth's surface is called
questions.explanation: Wind is moving air, caused by the Sun's uneven heating.

questions.question: On a sunny day, which usually heats up FASTER?

choices.C: They heat at the same speed

questions.explanation: Land heats up faster than water.

questions.question: Sunlight that strikes Earth straight-on, instead of at a slant, is called
questions.explanation: Light that strikes straight-on is direct sunlight, which the equator receives the most of.

questions.question: Large movements of ocean water around Earth are called
questions.explanation: Ocean currents are large movements of ocean water, driven partly by uneven solar heating.

questions.question: Which usually cools down FASTER after the Sun sets?

choices.C: They cool at exactly the same speed

questions.explanation: Land cools down faster than water, just as it heats up faster.

questions.question: How is sunlight at the equator DIFFERENT from sunlight at the poles?

choices.B: Equator sunlight is slanted; pole sunlight is direct
choices.D: Equator sunlight is direct and concentrated; pole sunlight is slanted and spread out

questions.explanation: The equator gets direct, concentrated sunlight while the poles get slanted, spread-out sunlight.

questions.question: What happens to warm air near the equator?

choices.D: It rises, and cooler air moves in to replace it

questions.explanation: Warm air near the equator rises and cooler air moves in to replace it, creating wind.

questions.question: Which is NOT caused by the Sun's uneven heating of Earth?
questions.explanation: Earthquakes come from movement inside Earth, not from the Sun's uneven heating, while wind, currents, and weather do.

questions.question: Why does the same amount of sunlight warm the poles LESS than the equator?

choices.A: At the poles the light is spread over more area, so each spot gets less energy
choices.B: The poles are closer to the Sun
choices.C: The Sun is brighter at the equator

questions.explanation: Slanted light at the poles is spread over more area, so each spot receives less energy and stays cooler.

questions.question: Which is an EXAMPLE of the Sun's energy causing movement?

choices.C: Wind blowing because warm air rises

questions.explanation: Wind blowing as warm air rises is an example of the Sun's energy causing movement.

questions.question: Which statement about the Sun and Earth is TRUE?

choices.A: The Sun heats every part of Earth exactly the same
choices.B: The poles receive the most direct sunlight
choices.C: Earth's round shape causes the Sun to heat it unevenly
choices.D: The Sun has no effect on wind

questions.explanation: Because Earth is round, sunlight strikes some places more directly than others, causing uneven heating.

questions.question: A breeze blows from the cool ocean toward the warm land during the day. This wind is caused mainly by

choices.D: the land and water heating at different speeds

questions.explanation: Land heats faster than water, so the uneven heating sets the air in motion, creating the breeze.

questions.question: Why is the equator warm all year long?

choices.A: It is the part of Earth farthest from the Sun
choices.B: The Sun only shines there at night
choices.D: It receives direct, concentrated sunlight throughout the year

questions.explanation: The equator gets direct, concentrated sunlight all year, keeping it warm.

questions.question: Which best describes the source of the energy that drives Earth's wind and weather?
questions.explanation: Energy from the Sun heats Earth unevenly and drives wind and weather.

questions.question: Two cities receive the same number of hours of daylight, but one near the equator is much hotter. The best reason is that

choices.A: sunlight has nothing to do with temperature
choices.B: the equator city is closer to the Moon
choices.C: the cooler city gets more direct sunlight
choices.D: the equator city gets more direct sunlight

questions.explanation: The city near the equator receives more direct, concentrated sunlight, so it is hotter.

questions.question: Which statement about land and water heating is FALSE?

choices.A: Land heats up faster than water
choices.B: Land cools down faster than water
choices.C: Water heats up and cools down faster than land
choices.D: The different heating speeds help create wind

questions.explanation: Land heats and cools faster than water, so saying water is the faster one is false.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a cause with its effect?

choices.C: Uneven solar heating — wind and ocean currents
choices.D: Slanted light at the equator — the hottest temperatures

questions.explanation: Uneven heating by the Sun causes wind and ocean currents.

questions.question: If Earth were flat and faced the Sun evenly, what would most likely happen to wind and weather?

choices.B: Wind would blow much harder everywhere
choices.C: The poles would become the hottest places
choices.D: There would be much less uneven heating to drive wind and weather

questions.explanation: Even heating would reduce the temperature differences that drive wind and weather, so there would be much less of both.

questions.question: Which is an EXAMPLE of land heating faster than water?

choices.A: At midday the beach sand burns your feet while the ocean stays cool
choices.B: The ocean boils while the sand stays cold
choices.C: The sand and water are always the same temperature

questions.explanation: Hot beach sand while the ocean stays cool shows land heating faster than water.

questions.question: Sunlight reaching the poles is spread over a LARGER area than the same sunlight at the equator. This means each spot at the poles receives
questions.explanation: When the same light is spread over more area, each spot receives less energy, so the poles get less heat.

questions.question: Which best explains why we have wind, ocean currents, and weather on Earth?

choices.D: The Sun heats Earth unevenly, setting air and water in motion

questions.explanation: Uneven heating by the Sun moves air and water, creating wind, ocean currents, and weather.

questions.question: Which describes why the poles stay cold even in summer?

choices.A: They are farther from the Sun than the equator by a huge distance
choices.C: Sunlight always reaches them at a low, slanted angle and spreads out

questions.explanation: Sunlight at the poles always arrives at a low, slanted angle and spreads out, so the poles stay cold.

questions.question: At night, a coastal breeze can blow from the land toward the water. One reason is that

choices.A: land cools down faster than water at night
choices.B: water cools faster than land at night
choices.C: the Sun heats the land at night
choices.D: the Moon pulls the air toward the water

questions.explanation: Land cools faster than water, so at night the temperature difference can reverse the breeze toward the water.

questions.question: Which is the MAIN source of energy for Earth's water cycle, plants, and weather?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the main source of energy for almost everything on Earth, including the water cycle, plants, and weather.

questions.question: Which question would BEST test the idea that land heats faster than water?

choices.A: Place soil and water in the Sun and measure which warms up faster
choices.B: Measure how heavy a rock is
choices.D: Check the color of the ocean

questions.explanation: Putting soil and water in the Sun and timing which warms faster directly tests whether land heats faster than water.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the equator and the poles?

choices.A: The poles are warmer because they get direct sunlight
choices.B: Both receive sunlight at the same angle
choices.C: The equator is warmer because it gets direct, concentrated sunlight

questions.explanation: The equator is warmer because it receives direct, concentrated sunlight, while the poles get slanted light.

questions.question: A student claims, "Wind happens because the Sun heats all of Earth's air evenly." This claim is

choices.B: incorrect, wind comes from UNEVEN heating that makes air move
choices.C: correct, the Sun heats everything the same
choices.D: incorrect, the Sun does not heat the air at all

questions.explanation: Wind is caused by uneven heating that makes warm air rise and cooler air move in, not by even heating.

questions.question: Which best explains the connection between the Sun and ocean currents?

choices.A: Ocean currents depend only on the color of the water
choices.B: The Sun freezes the ocean evenly
choices.C: Ocean currents come from the inner core spinning
choices.D: The Sun heats ocean water unevenly, helping set the water in motion

questions.explanation: Uneven heating of ocean water by the Sun helps drive ocean currents.

questions.question: Which describes the path of energy that leads to weather?

choices.A: Earthquake energy moves air and water to make weather
choices.B: The Moon's light moves the air to make weather
choices.C: The Sun heats Earth unevenly, which moves air and water and produces weather
choices.D: Minerals heat the air to make weather

questions.explanation: The Sun heats Earth unevenly, which moves air and water and produces weather.
